status: Adopted minimal guard; focused build, typecheck and correctness checks passed
change: PlaybackClock.sample validates its argument and absence of observations first, then returns its current value for now <= sampled without moving the host-time baseline. No timers, public API, interpolation math, authority observation, rates, delay, queue or render settings changed.
cause: The previous implementation clamped a negative sample interval to zero but still assigned sampled=now. A stale callback therefore did not immediately move the presentation, yet the next current callback consumed part of an already-consumed interval again. Simulation time was already monotonic; explicit reverse seeking is separately supported by Replica.at(time).

independentReference.description: Permanent fixture contains the full pre-change compiled PlaybackClock, with unrelated module import and following Replica removed. Actual class source equals the ignored original full-module class. Removing only the adopted source guard restores the original playback.ts hash.
independentReference.ordinaryCoverage: 7,200 increasing/equal timestamp positions, 14,400 sample calls per implementation, across delays 0/.1/.3/2 seconds, .55/.85/1.1 authority rates, calibration, long gaps and resets. Float64 result bytes and complete clock own state match the frozen reference.
independentReference.additionalCoverage: Stale timestamp, actual Replica output, equal timestamp after a new cause, finite-argument validation before any observation, held-at-latest packet gaps, reset to an earlier epoch and explicit reverse Replica.at seeking.

visibleProof.description: A confirmed latest cause at simulation time 1 second and host time 0; samples at host seconds [0,.02,.01,.03], compared with [0,.02,.03]. Replica projects x=10*time; canonical CausalReceiver uses its actual publisher/fixture with x=4*time and sampled audio RPM.
visibleProof.actualCanonicalConsumer: The unchanged canonical CausalReceiver with its default production Engine clock exactly matches the complete no-stale presentation object. Injecting the independent old clock reproduces the position and audio difference.

limits: This demonstrates an externally observable timestamp-order correctness defect and its bounded correction. It does not establish the frequency of stale live callbacks, screenshot attribution, native GPU behavior, FPS, allocation or whole-server gains. No Game production source was edited; canonical consumer validation executes actual classes directly without a browser or server.
